data.topic: Should employers be allowed to use AI systems to monitor employees' work?
data.audience: The management board and staff representatives of a mid-sized logistics company
data.claim: Employers should be allowed to use AI systems to monitor employees' work.

arguments.reason: AI monitoring can make dangerous workplaces safer.
arguments.evidence: In Case A, "Forklift accidents fell during the same period".

arguments.reason: Monitoring data can make performance reviews fairer.
arguments.evidence: My uncle's company uses tracking data in reviews and he says it is more objective.
arguments.warrant: Data is less biased than a manager's memory.

counters.counter: Staff representatives may argue that monitoring damages trust between workers and managers.
counters.response: Trust is less important than safety.

data.draft: Employers should be allowed to use AI systems to monitor employees' work. First, AI monitoring makes workplaces safer. In Case A, forklift accidents fell after the system was introduced. Second, monitoring data makes performance reviews fairer, because data is less biased than a manager's memory. Some people say monitoring damages trust, but trust is less important than safety. Therefore, companies should use AI monitoring.
